title: Bringing the band to the Swing coffee house
summary: The band arrives and the Japanese fans are awed; a listening concert follows.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Right. And Jaffe said, you go first. And behind me stood Lewis and George Lewis and Nelson and the rest of the band. So I knocked on the door of the Swing. The door opened and little Sayori Yamamoto appears. And she looked at me and again, in very hesitant English, said, do you have the autograph? I said, no, but I have George Lewis. And the door opened and George Lewis came in. The place suddenly you could hear just a collective gasp. Everything stopped. And the musicians ended. And within ten seconds there wasn't standing room in that place. It filled with young Japanese who had never seen anything like it. And the band sat down at a couple of tables against the wall. Places were made for them. And it was almost a religious education. The man that this shrine had been built for had suddenly walked into it. And the adoration was, you could really feel it, which may have embarrassed George possibly. It was so obvious. They sat down and then began one of the loveliest jazz concerts I've ever heard. Because these men, without their instruments, sat there. And now over the vitrola, over the phonograph, came the sounds of George Lewis and Jim Robinson and whoever, but always George. And after each solo, the Japanese, in the swing, clapped. And the musician who took the solo, who was George Lewis, he stood up and took a bow. And this went on for about an hour and a half. The following morning, I must say, I walked through that little part of Tokyo and I think I could have run for mayor. Every Japanese, Konichiwa, Ohio, Gazzaro, nodded. And I said hello. I never realized I had so many friends. Then eventually, the following night, in order that the other swing coffee shop did not lose face, we went over there and paid a repeat visit. Of course, it was not a surprise because obviously they had been on the phone immediately.
